# Neon Design System

The design system for Unified Home Portal and beyond

## Dependencies
Neon is written and tested in these versions.
 * npm:	8.9.0
 * node: 16.14.0

## Getting started

* Make sure you have permission to see these files by going to https://gitlab.com/powerschoolgroup/neon/neon-design-system
* In gitbash run `git clone git@gitlab.com:powerschoolgroup/neon/neon-design-system.git`
  * If you haven't set up your computer to communicate with gitlab yet there will be instructions at the bottom of this document.
* Get an Artifactory identity token by doing the following:
  * In your browser go here: https://artifactory.powerschoolcorp.com/
  * Click "Log in" in the top right corner
  * Press the SAML SSO button in the "Or Sign In With" section
  * Sign in with MS if prompted
  * In the top corner, click "Welcome {your email}"
  * Selected "Edit Profile"
  * Press the "Generate an Identity Token" button
  * Press the copy button to copy the key to the clipboard.
  * From any directory run the following
    * npm config set _authToken=YOUR_ARTIFACTORY_IDENTITY_TOKEN_GOES_HERE
    * npm config set registry=https://artifactory.powerschoolcorp.com/artifactory/api/npm/npm
    * npm config set always-auth=true
    * close all of your terminals and re-open them.
      * If it still doesn't work you might even just try restarting your computer.
* cd into neon-design-system and run **npm install**
* cd into neon-design-system and run **npm run dev**
* in your browser look at http://localhost:8080

## Neon Specific Best Practices

### Injection Principles
This section deals with rules regarding code from outside of neon getting injected 

#### Spacing
* Spacing around a container should be done by adding a class.
* The class should be prefixed with "&#95;&#95;neon&#95;&#95;"
* Adding an additional class of &#95;&#95;neon&#95;&#95;flush-top, &#95;&#95;neon&#95;&#95;flush-right, &#95;&#95;neon&#95;&#95;flush-bottom, &#95;&#95;neon&#95;&#95;flush-left will zero out the spacing in the direction indicated.
* Spacing classes on injected content should be added by the injected content. That way they can still have full width content as necessary.
* In general, web components should add the class automatically and provide the ability to turn it off.
* There should be a separate spacing class for each type of injected content

Spacing Visual Documentation: https://lucid.app/lucidchart/2943997e-786d-4f20-b553-5efdcf61348f/edit?viewport_loc=-37%2C1447%2C2434%2C1183%2CER~URvz0OmhA&invitationId=inv_4945dea9-e589-42ce-a29f-72ea546bf9bb

### Web Components

The developer experience will be much nicer if we adhere to some rules which will make things consistent from component to component.

#### Web Components - SCSS
- Each widget scss file must be scoped to the element name.  This prevents styles from being used outside of the widget.  Also, since things are scoped, it is OK to style native elements like buttons without using classes if you would like to.
- Class names within a scoped component should start with neon-{component-name}-.  Do not use class names starting with '&#95;&#95;neon&#95;&#95;' unless they will not be scoped by the web component.
- Class names must be completely spelled out and should not be constructed using the '&' character.  
  - This will not pass code review: .my-button { &-large{ height: 100px; }}
  - This will pass code review: .my-button-large { height: 100px; }
- Every scss file in a widget directory should minimize dependencies on other scss files.


#### Web Components - RTL Support
- When creating new components be conscious of "left" and "right" usage in css properties when they differ.
- If only one left/right is used, or when both are used but different, we want to use logistical properties instead
 - https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_Logical_Properties
 - https://www.w3.org/TR/css-logical-1/
- see http://localhost:8080/css/rtl for additional information 

#### Web Components - Function Names

- Function names that start with "get" should return something.
- Function names that start with "is" should return a boolean.
- Function names that start with "set" should take in an argument and set something in the class.
- Function names that start with "render" should return an HTMLElement or Array&lt;HTMLElement&gt;
- Function names that start with "renderConditional" should return a ConditionalElement or Array&lt;ConditionalElement&gt;
- Function names that start with "draw" or "redraw" should return undefined and do DOM manipulation; either updating existing DOM elements, or calling render functions and adding it to existing DOM elements.
- Libraries of static functions in the shared directory should not be in classes but instead, export the functions directly. This allows webpack to optimize file sizes.

#### Web Components - Custom Event Names
- Custom Event Names should be camelCase (no dashes)
- Custom Event Names should start with 'neon'
- Custom Event names should not have the word "event" in them.
  - Example: neonLayoutDetailClose
- If an event is fired as a result of another event being listened to, use the present tense.
  - Example: neonLayoutDetailClose
  - Example: neonGlobalSearchTextChange

#### Web Components - Firing/Dispatching Events
- Our normal way of communicating with outside code in a web component is by firing events.
- Events should only be fired/dispatched when the user interacts directly with an element in the component.
- Web components should not fire events just because one of its attributes or properties changes.  (This can create performance issues.)

#### Web Components - Attributes and Classes on Component Tag
- Attributes on the component tag starting with "data-" are assumed to be inputs into the widget.
- Classes on the component tag are assumed to be added by the developer using the widget.
- Due to those assumptions, it is best practice not to add classes or attributes to the widget tag.  A way around it is to use a div that wraps everything within the widget and then apply your classes and attributes to that div.
##### Example
When you see this in the DOM explorer in Chrome here are the assumptions about it.  

    <__neon__super-icon class="my-special-icon" data-type="super-big">
      <div class="big" data-count="15">
        ...
      </div>
    </__neon__super-icon>

- The class "my-special-icon" was put on there by the developer using the widget, not by the JavaScript in NeonSuperIcon.
- The attribute data-type="super-big" is an input into the widget and was not set there by the JavaScript in NeonSuperIcon code.
- The class "big" was put in there by the JavaScript in NeonSuperIcon code.
- The attribute "data-count" was set by the JavaScript in NeonSuperIcon.


#### Web Components - Dealing With dependencies (discussed by the entire team on 6/14/2022)
- Web components can use other web components.
  - It provides a smaller file size since css does not have to be duplicated.
  - Using the separate component guarantees it will look like the component is intended to look.
  - Using the component will more closely follow the design system the designers are using in Figma or whatever library they change to in 2023.

##### Web Components - Testing for Inherited Styles
- We have a local .inherited-garbage class that should be added to a direct parent of our components in the demo tab of their page.
- Use this as a text to see what styles bleed in from an ancestor and make necessary corrections in that component's styles
- see the button-page.tsx as an example 


##### Web Components - Using dependent component rules
  - The dependent component needs to be able to be used without altering its css from the super component.  If changes are necessary, add a new option as an input to the component, or don't use the component.

#### Web Components - Slots and Spacing
  - The web component must provide spacing around the injected slot by default.
  - The implementing developer must have the option to turn off the spacing add a class inside the injected content.
  - The spacing class should be named &#95;&#95;neon&#95;&#95;{component-name}-{slot-name}
  - Do not apply anything but padding to the spacing class.

#### Web Components - Pass Through Input names
Sometimes a component needs to create an input that it will "pass through" to a child component.  An example of this is when a component has a sub component of neon-avatar.
The attribute it would create to pass through to the avatar first name would be data-avatar-first-name.
So the pattern is `data-${child-component-name}-${child-component-attribute-name}`

#### Web Components - ids
Please do not use document.getElementById inside web components to refer to the component's internals. Please use this.querySelector(# + {the-element-id}) instead.  This should make it so even if there are duplicate ids on the page, that the component gets the sub element inside it like it is supposed to.  We do ask teams to pass in unique ids, but they don't always do that.

### SASS Components

- Do not style native elements without a class attached to them.  
  - button { background: blue; } //DO NOT DO THIS
  - button.neon-special-button { background: blue; } //This is ok because it only styles buttons with that class on it.

## Code Review Frequent corrections
* `!== null`, `!== undefined`, `=== null`, and `=== undefined` are not allowed. Please use `!= null` or `== null`.
* Put types on the variables that you define because it makes the code much easier to read in the gitlab code review interface.
  * Types on arguments in function definitions are especially important.
  * Some patterns in React such as the pattern for useState do not need types directly on the variable because you put the type into the useState function you are calling. const [myStateVar, setMyStateVar] = useState<string>('hello');
* Don't use .forEach() because for-of and for-i loops execute faster.
* This pattern is more verbose than it needs to be: `return someCondition ? true : false;`
  * Use `return someCondition;` instead.

## How to setup ssh key in Gitlab
* Open GitBash - https://git-scm.com/downloads
* Type :  ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -C "userEmailAddress@powerschool.com"
* Whenever asked to type : press Enter to choose defaults
* There would be two files created (id_rsa & id_rsa.pub) with public (Type: Microsoft Publisher Documents)
* Now go to the mentioned file location at your local computer and copy the ssh key (Public Key).
* Login into GitLab -> Profile Settings -> SSH Keys
* In the "Key" field paste the copied public key and Title will be your PowerSchool id, then click on Add Key
